# 1. PDF files of the project folder

The provenance P2 of the main project lists the nine published papers of the project
folder, with their checksums, and states which were used for what. **The revision used
no PDF file of the project folder anew.** It builds on the documents and programs of
the main project, which rest on those papers as P2 describes; the hypotheses of the
revision are the author's instructions of November 12, 2026 (provenance RP0), not a
passage of a paper.

# 2. Literature used for the first time in the revision

The following papers were used. They are not in the project folder; their
bibliographic data were verified by a search of the web on November 12, 2026, and the
numbers taken from them are those stated in the right-hand column.

| reference | what was taken from it | used in |
|:----------|:---------|:---|
| F. Hofmann and J. Müller, *Relativistic tests with lunar laser ranging*, Class. Quantum Grav. **35**, 035015 (2018) | the rate of change of Newton's constant, $(7.1\pm7.6)\times10^{-14}$ per year | RS3, Sec. 3 |
| J. Alvey, N. Sabti, M. Escudero and M. Fairbairn, *Improved BBN constraints on the variation of the gravitational constant*, Eur. Phys. J. C **80**, 148 (2020) | Newton's constant at nucleosynthesis over its present value, $0.99^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$ (two sigma) | RS3, Sec. 3 |
| R. Lange et al., *Improved limits for violations of local position invariance from atomic clock comparisons*, Phys. Rev. Lett. **126**, 011102 (2021) | rates of change of the fine-structure constant, $1.0(1.1)\times10^{-18}$ per year, and of the ratio of the proton mass to the electron mass, $-8(36)\times10^{-18}$ per year | RS2, Sec. 5; RS3, Sec. 3 |
| R. J. Scherrer and D. N. Spergel, *How constant is the Fermi coupling constant?*, Phys. Rev. D **47**, 4774 (1993) | nucleosynthesis allows the Fermi constant, at fixed fermion masses, to differ by about 10 to 20 per cent from its present value | RS3, Sec. 3 |
| E. W. Kolb, M. J. Perry and T. P. Walker, *Time variation of fundamental constants, primordial nucleosynthesis, and the size of extra dimensions*, Phys. Rev. D **33**, 869 (1986) | cited for the idea; no number taken | RS3, Sec. 1 |
| D. Chirkov, S. Pavluchenko and A. Toporensky, *Exact exponential solutions in Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet flat anisotropic cosmology*, Mod. Phys. Lett. A **29**, 1450093 (2014) | cited for the class of solutions; the solution of DMD, Sec. 1.4a, was computed independently | DMD, Sec. 1.4a |

Standard results that are used without a specific source — the Fermi–Dirac and
Bose–Einstein spectra of particle creation on an exponentially changing background,
the Gibbons–Hawking temperature of de Sitter space, the recurrence relations of the
Bessel functions, the weak-coupling ratios of the theory of Bardeen, Cooper and
Schrieffer — are derived or verified numerically in the documents where they appear.
